chapters.title: Okay fine, the fix (Bom made me)

chapters.first-impression: Okay, Gap. Here's what people clock in the first ten seconds: confidence, opinions, and posture like you're about to give a talk nobody booked. You walk in like the room should rearrange itself around you. Half the time it does, which is annoying for everyone else and great for you. People assume you're in charge, so they hand you things: projects, problems, the restaurant booking. You take them, obviously. What they don't see right away is that you're quite sensitive about being respected. You'd rather be right than liked. You'd prefer both. And you get grumpy when you can only pick one. That's the read. You're welcome.
chapters.your-red-flag: Your red flag? You don't bend. At all. A tree grows straight up, and you've decided that's a personality trait instead of a botanical fact. You'll listen to feedback, nod thoughtfully, and then do exactly what you'd already planned. You call it conviction. Everyone else calls it the reason they say can someone else talk to Gap. Being stubborn about values is admirable. Being stubborn about which route to the cinema is just tiring for the people in the car. Bom says you're principled. I say you're principled about things that are not principles. Learn the difference and you'll be unstoppable instead of merely unmovable.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gap. Gap enters a party like it's a board meeting.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: That's called leadership, Yeon.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: It's called refusing to let anyone else pick the restaurant.

chapters.first-impression: Eul, people meet you and think: oh, they're lovely. Easy to talk to, warm, funny, somehow already on first-name terms with the barista. You read rooms like a professional and adjust in real time. Ten seconds in, people feel comfortable. Ten minutes in, they've told you about their childhood and their ex. What they don't notice is that you're also quietly checking whether they like you. Constantly. You're charming partly because you're working at it, a little, all the time. Which is fine. Just know that it's work, and you're allowed to clock out whenever you like.
chapters.your-red-flag: Your red flag: you're a professional chameleon. You become whatever the person in front of you seems to want, and you're so good at it that you sometimes forget your own color. I don't mind, whatever you want. You do mind. You mind a lot, three days later, in the shower, rehearsing what you should have said. You call it being flexible. It's actually avoiding conflict with a smile. And eventually the resentment leaks out sideways, in some weird little comment, and everyone's confused about where it came from. Have the opinion at the time. It's cheaper.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul. You've said 'I don't mind' eleven times today.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul is just easygoing!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul keeps a secret list of every compromise. I've seen it.

chapters.first-impression: Byeong, you don't enter a room, you happen to it. Ten seconds in, people know your name, your opinion on the playlist, and that you're the fun one. You're warm, generous, a little loud, and genuinely delightful. People feel seen by you, which is your real magic. What they also clock: you need an audience. Not in a bad way. You just light up when people are watching and dim slightly when they're not. That isn't vanity. That's a sun noticing it's daytime. Still, it's worth knowing that everyone can tell when you're on.
chapters.your-red-flag: Red flag, Byeong: you overshare, overcommit and overexplain, all before lunch. You say yes to every plan because you love people, then cancel two of them because you're exhausted. You're honest to the point of did you really have to say that at the table. And when you're hurt, you don't hide it. The whole room gets the weather report, with satellite images. Openness is lovely. A little filter is also lovely. You're allowed to have both. They're not mutually exclusive, no matter what your mouth has been telling you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, you said yes to four plans tonight. It's Tuesday.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong just loves people!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Loves people, then cancels by voice note. From the bath.

chapters.first-impression: Jeong, people meet you and feel like you're paying attention. Because you are. Ten seconds in, you've noticed their mood, their nervous hands, and that the person beside them is lying about something. You're warm but not loud, a candle rather than a bonfire. People feel safe telling you things. What they don't see: you're also deciding whether they're safe for you. And most of them don't pass. You're friendly with many and close to very few, and the few have no idea how hard the exam was. Maybe make the exam a little easier.
chapters.your-red-flag: Red flag, Jeong: you overthink. Professionally. One ambiguous text and you've written a three-act play, cast it, and cried at the ending. You also hold onto hurts, quietly, for years. You'll say it's fine and then remember the exact date it wasn't. And your mood can change the temperature of a room without you saying a single word. You don't need to stop feeling deeply. Please don't. You need to tell people what you feel before it hardens into a grudge they didn't know they were earning. Say it small and early. It's kinder.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Jeong. You've reread that text nine times. It says 'ok'.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong is just very perceptive!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Perceptive, yes. Also writing a tragedy about a full stop.

chapters.first-impression: Mu, new people tend to feel calmer. You're solid, unbothered, the human equivalent of a very good sofa. Ten seconds in they think: this person could handle a crisis. You could, and you have, several times, without making a fuss. You don't perform, don't oversell, don't rush. What they also clock: you're hard to read. Is Mu happy? Annoyed? Asleep with eyes open? Nobody knows. Not even, on some days, you. You've perfected the neutral face so well that you sometimes forget there's weather behind it. Let someone in on the forecast sometimes.
chapters.your-red-flag: Here's the flag: you don't move. Physically, emotionally, philosophically. You've had the same opinion since 2014 and you're proud of it. New idea? You'll consider it. For about two years. And when you're upset, you go silent and heavy, like weather that refuses to break, while everyone tiptoes around the mountain wondering what they did. Stability is a real gift. Stubbornness dressed up as stability is just stubbornness with better posture. Learn which one you're doing, and admit it when it's the second. Hint: if you can't explain why, it's probably the second one.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, that opinion is old enough to have its own birthday.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: That's called being consistent!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: It's called refusing to try the new café. For three years.

chapters.first-impression: Gi, new people tend to want to tell you everything. You're warm, practical, with strong mom-friend energy whatever your age. Ten seconds in, you've offered them water, a snack, or a solution. You notice who's uncomfortable and quietly fix it. What they don't see: you're also worrying. About them, about the plan, about whether you said something weird three minutes ago. Your brain runs a background app called What Could Go Wrong, and it never closes. Not even on holiday. Especially not on holiday. Maybe close a few tabs before bed.
chapters.your-red-flag: Here's the flag: you overgive, then quietly resent it. You'll do the favor, the planning, the emotional heavy lifting, and say it's no trouble at all. Then one day you snap about the dishes and everyone's shocked. It was never about the dishes. It was the last forty things. You also worry so much that you sometimes control. I'm just helping can mean I'm managing you. Let people fail a little. It builds character. Theirs, not yours. Yours is already very well built, thank you. Say the small annoyance when it's still small, before it turns into a dishwasher incident.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gi. You've apologized six times today. For existing.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi is just considerate!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gi runs a free care service with no opening hours.

chapters.first-impression: Gyeong, strangers feel slightly intimidated, then slightly impressed. You're direct, decisive, and you don't fake interest in anything. Ten seconds in, they know whether you like them, because your face has no privacy settings. You're loyal, fair, and you'd fight for your people without being asked. What they don't see right away: you're actually soft about the few you love. Very soft. You just guard it like a bank vault with a moat and a slightly scary security guard, who is also you. Maybe lower the drawbridge occasionally.
chapters.your-red-flag: Let's start with the red one: you're blunt. Sometimes surgically. You say the true thing with zero padding and then can't understand why someone's upset. I was just being honest. Yes. Honesty without kindness is just a sharp object being waved around a kitchen. You also see the world in black and white, and gray makes you angry. Most of life is gray. Annoying, I know. You can keep the blade. Just learn to put it back in its sheath when you're having a conversation instead of a duel. Same truth, gentler delivery. Still counts.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, you called their haircut 'a choice'. They cried.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gyeong was just being honest.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Honesty without kindness is a knife in a nice outfit.

chapters.first-impression: Sin, strangers think: put together. The outfit, the posture, the very specific coffee order. You notice everything and you're polite about it, mostly. Ten seconds in, people can tell you have taste, and maybe also that you're slightly judging their shoes. You are. We both know you are. What they don't see: you're sensitive. Very. A careless comment can sting for days behind a perfectly composed face, and you'll replay it while doing your skincare, word by word. Maybe tell someone when it happens, out loud, on the day.
chapters.your-red-flag: Let's start with the red one: perfectionism with a side of silent judgment. You have standards for everything, and you grade everyone quietly, then feel disappointed when they fail criteria they didn't know existed. You also take small slights personally and keep them polished in a little display case, lit nicely, labeled by date. People think you're cool and above it. Actually, you're hurt and far too elegant to say so. That's a lot of energy spent on looking unbothered when you could just mention it. Saying that stung is extremely chic, actually.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Sin. You've judged three outfits and a font since we started.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin just has great taste!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Great taste. And a secret scorecard nobody agreed to.

chapters.first-impression: Im, at a first meeting people feel like they've walked into a fun, slightly elusive story. You're curious, clever, adventurous, with three fascinating anecdotes and a trip coming up. Ten seconds in, they want to know you. Ten weeks in, they're still trying to pin you down. What they don't see: your mind is always somewhere else, half planning the next thing, the next city, the next idea. You're present, mostly. About eighty percent. The other twenty is already boarding a different flight. It's charming. It's also very obvious to everyone sitting with you.
chapters.your-red-flag: The flag Yeon sees first: you disappear. Not dramatically. You just drift, stop replying, go and do your own thing for a week, then come back like nothing happened. To you, it's freedom. To everyone else, it's a slightly anxious are we okay? You also avoid commitment like it's a parking ticket. And you can turn cool when things get emotional, retreating into logic. Let's think about this rationally is not a hug. Nobody in tears has ever wanted a flowchart. A two-line heads-up before you vanish would solve about ninety percent of this.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im. You replied to my message from March. It's not March.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Im is just very free-spirited!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Free-spirited. Also emotionally on another continent.

chapters.first-impression: Gye, at a first meeting people feel oddly understood. You're gentle, observant, a little mysterious, with soft energy that makes people relax without knowing why. Ten seconds in, you've picked up their mood and matched it. They feel like you get them. You do. What they don't see: you've also absorbed their stress, and you'll carry it home like a souvenir nobody asked you to buy. You're basically a sponge in a nice jumper, and you go home much heavier than you arrived. Wring yourself out before bed. Seriously, every night.
chapters.your-red-flag: The flag Yeon sees first: you're vague. Maybe. We'll see. Whatever you want. You hint instead of asking, then feel hurt when nobody picks up on the hint. You also retreat into your imagination when life gets hard, which is cozy but isn't a plan. And you can be a bit secretive, sharing the weather report but never the forecast. Mystery is charming on a first date. By month six, it's just confusing, and the people who love you are tired of guessing. Give them the forecast. They can handle it, I promise.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gye. 'Maybe' is not an answer. It's a fog machine.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye is just gentle!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gentle, and expecting everyone to be psychic. They're not.
